layers.label: U.S. House
layers.rank_note: 10 congressional districts — the largest districts Washington carries below the state itself

source.answers: The U.S. House district covering the point, and the representative holding it.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 0 (120th Congressional Districts), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 10 features for Washington, measured 2026-11-11. Layer 4, the 119th Congress's map, draws the same 10 districts (every district's IoU 1.0, measured that day), because Washington's map is still the one its Redistricting Commission drew after the 2020 census, so nothing changes on 3 January 2027; the builder measures both and refuses to write if they ever differ before that date. Simplified together with the legislative map, by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval, and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: congress-roster.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the public-domain unitedstates/congress-legislators dataset — including each member's district office and Washington office.

layers.label: County
layers.rank_note: 39 counties, pre-built from TIGERweb; the instance's offline anchor layer, larger on average than a legislative district

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — State_County, layer 1, pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 39 features, measured 2026-11-11.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER YET. Each Washington county is governed by an elected board of county commissioners unless its home-rule charter sets up another government, as King County's does (an elected county executive and county council), and elects officers such as an assessor, an auditor, a prosecuting attorney, a sheriff and a treasurer; no list of them was read in this pass, so the card names the county only. Recorded as gap wa-county-officials.

layers.label: Washington Senate District
layers.rank_note: 49 legislative districts, each electing one senator — smaller on average than a county

source.answers: The legislative district covering the point, and the senator it elects.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 1 (2026 State Legislative Districts - Upper), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 49 features, measured 2026-11-11: the plan the Washington State Redistricting Commission drew after the 2020 census. Washington elects both chambers from the same 49 legislative districts, and TIGERweb's layer 2 (2026 State Legislative Districts - Lower) draws exactly the same districts (every district's IoU 1.0, measured on every build), so ONE file, wa-legislative-districts.json, serves the Senate and the House layers alike. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: wa-senate-members.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the Legislature's own site (leg.wa.gov): each senator's name, district and party from the Legislature's list of members, and the Olympia office and telephone from the senator's own page, as that page prints them. The pages link an e-mail form for each member rather than printing an address, so none is shown.

layers.label: Washington House District
layers.rank_note: the same 49 legislative districts as the Senate, each electing two representatives

source.answers: The legislative district covering the point, and the two representatives it elects.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 1 (2026 State Legislative Districts - Upper), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 49 features, measured 2026-11-11: the plan the Washington State Redistricting Commission drew after the 2020 census. Washington elects both chambers from the same 49 legislative districts, and TIGERweb's layer 2 (2026 State Legislative Districts - Lower) draws exactly the same districts (every district's IoU 1.0, measured on every build), so ONE file, wa-legislative-districts.json, serves the Senate and the House layers alike. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: wa-house-members.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the Legislature's own site (leg.wa.gov): both representatives of each district, Position 1 and Position 2, with each one's party from the Legislature's list of members and Olympia office and telephone from the member's own page. A district the list shows with fewer than two members is shipped with the members it lists and the date it was read, and the card says the other seat is not listed.

layers.label: School District
layers.rank_note: 295 school districts, drawn from a tile archive mirrored from TIGERweb

source.answers: The public school district covering the point.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — School, layer 0 (unified school districts), mirrored into a vector-tile archive this site serves (scripts/mirror_tiger_tiles.py); 295 features for Washington, measured 2026-11-11. TIGERweb's secondary and elementary layers carry nothing for Washington, so they are not drawn.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER YET. Each school district is governed by an elected board of directors, and no list of the members was read in this pass — recorded as gap wa-school-board-members.

layers.label: ZIP Code
layers.rank_note: ZIP Code Tabulation Areas inside Washington, drawn from a tile archive of the ones inside the state; the layer hides outside it

source.answers: The ZIP Code Tabulation Area covering the point — the Census Bureau's areal approximation of the USPS delivery routes sharing a ZIP code, not a postal boundary.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — ZIP Code Tabulation Areas, layer 11 of the PUMA/TAD/TAZ/UGA/ZCTA service, mirrored into a vector-tile archive of the ZCTAs inside Washington (scripts/mirror_tiger_tiles.py). ZCTAs carry NO STATE FIELD because they cross state lines, so this is the one TIGERweb layer here fetched by a bounding ENVELOPE rather than STATE='53'. 740 features in the app's box, which reaches into Oregon and Idaho, 606 of them inside or reaching into Washington and kept in the archive, measured 2026-11-11.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a ZIP code is a mail-routing convenience, not a unit of government, so nobody is elected from one. The card says what the boundary actually is rather than leaving a reader to assume it means more.
source.applies: Washington. The layer is hidden outside the state outline, because outside it the Census's point query answers with a neighbouring state's real ZIP code.

layers.label: City or Town
layers.rank_note: 281 incorporated cities and towns, drawn from a tile archive mirrored from TIGERweb

source.answers: The incorporated city or town containing the point, or that the point is outside every one.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Places_CouSub_ConCity_SubMCD, layer 4 (incorporated places), mirrored into a vector-tile archive this site serves (scripts/mirror_tiger_tiles.py); 281 features for Washington, measured 2026-11-11: 212 cities and 69 towns, every one recorded as an active government. MOST OF WASHINGTON IS IN NO CITY OR TOWN (2.6% of its land, 4,503.5 of 172,121.7 km2, is inside one), and there the county is the general-purpose local government, so an empty card says the point is outside every one rather than naming a place. Washington's county subdivisions are census county divisions and its census-designated places statistical areas, neither with a government, so neither is drawn.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER YET. No statewide roster of Washington's mayors and council members has been read for this app, so the card names no one rather than guessing. Recorded as gap wa-municipal-officeholders.

layers.label: Police Station
layers.rank_note: nearest police stations by straight-line distance — a point layer, ranked with the other nearest-N layers

source.answers: The three nearest police stations to the point, by straight-line distance, with each one's address.

boundary.label: USGS The National Map — structures layer 53 (Police Stations), queried live at runtime by a bounding envelope through the paged loader. Public domain. Measured 2026-11-11: 318 points in Washington's envelope, under the service's 2,000-record cap, and paged anyway so that stops being a fact anyone has to re-check.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a police station is a facility, not an elected district. Nobody is elected from one.
source.applies: Washington — plus the border strip its envelope necessarily includes. A BUILDING, NOT A JURISDICTION: which agency answers at a given point is a service-area question this instance has not been researched for, so the card says where the nearest are and never who serves you. Nearest-three is a proximity fact, so for a reader near the state line the nearest one really may be in a neighbouring state, and the card's intro says these are straight-line distances.

anchor_point.note: The Legislative Building, Olympia, Thurston County. Measured 2026-11-11 against the shipped files: 3,815 m inside its legislative district and 13,515 m inside its congressional district and county.

negative_point.note: Victoria, British Columbia, across the Strait of Juan de Fuca — outside Washington and outside every other instance in the fleet, and inside permalink_gate so the app answers the click and every shipped layer correctly returns nothing. Measured 2026-11-11: TIGERweb's state layer places it in no state (control: the Legislative Building in Olympia returns Washington), none of the state's shipped boundary files contains it, and none of the outlines in fleet-outlines.json does. IT IS IN CANADA, SO NO NEIGHBOUR'S GO-LIVE MOVES IT.

geometry.note: The whole-Washington outline for the coverage wash (loadMetroOutline), dissolved from the county fabric (39 counties).
The 39 counties — the instance's offline anchor layer and the ground the coverage tests use.
The 10 U.S. House districts, TIGERweb layer 0 (CD120), the same map as layer 4 (the 119th Congress), so nothing changes on 3 January 2027.

The 49 Washington legislative districts, TIGERweb layer 1 (2026 State Legislative Districts, identical to layer 2). Both the Senate and the House layers read this one file, because Washington elects both chambers from the same districts.

The ZIP code search index (scripts/build_zip_index.mjs): one Point per ZIP code the app's ZIP layer draws, at the spot inside it on the layer's own ground farthest from every edge, with its extent and its layer, so a ZIP code typed into the search box selects that spot, turns the ZIP layer on and pins it for comparison (ENGINE geocoder-search, showZip). A ZIP code with no spot 75 m clear of every edge is left out, and one that crosses into another app's state is listed by whichever app holds more of it. GENERATED from data/app/tiles/zip-code.pmtiles, with each spot inside metro-outline.json (the outline its coverage test reads); --check rebuilds it from the committed archive and outline. Exact count, because it changes only when the Census Bureau changes its ZIP Code Tabulation Areas, and that wants reading rather than a widened bound.

rosters.note: U.S. House (WA) roster, refreshed weekly by update-wa-congress-roster.yml.
Washington Senate roster from the Legislature's own list of members and member pages (leg.wa.gov), one record per district, refreshed weekly.
Washington House roster from the Legislature's own list of members and member pages (leg.wa.gov), one record per district holding both of its representatives, refreshed weekly.
The recorded gaps this instance ships with, rendered by the data-gaps panel.

The officers Washington elects statewide and its two U.S. senators: state, officers (office, name, the office's own website, the day the name was last checked there) and usSenate. Built weekly by scripts/build_statewide_officials.py from wa/data/source/statewide-officials.source.json, which lists each office, the name and the page that must print it; the build reads robots.txt before every page, refuses to write when a page it read no longer prints the name, keeps the last checked record when a page cannot be read, and takes the senators from senate.gov's own list. Network-first: a name can change.
